Scope: Bounded structural Wikitext parsing and sanitized HTML rendering; no complete MediaWiki HTML parity claim.

Architecture.Expansion: MediaWikiTemplateExpander runs first with historical provenance and unchanged budgets.
Architecture.Parsing: MediaWikiWikitextRenderer.Parser creates a typed block/inline AST after expansion.

AuditFindings.Evidence: Existing parser recognizes matching delimiter levels 1 through 6 and routes content through safe inline rendering.
Existing typed list tree renderer produces balanced ul/ol structures within parse-depth and block bounds.
A confirmed marker-selection defect was fixed; the marker at each nesting level now selects that level's list tag, so *# produces an ordered child under an unordered parent.
A confirmed paragraph-classification defect was fixed; ; term and : definition lines now produce a typed dl/dt/dd block instead of paragraph text.
Existing typed parser and renderer cover table boundaries, rows, headers, cells, captions, spans, nested tables, and malformed-input diagnostics.
Only bounded allow-listed attributes are emitted; styles, event handlers, unsafe URLs, unsupported attributes, and excessive values are rejected or ignored.
Existing imported-page/media resolution and HTTP/HTTPS URL policy remain unchanged and covered by tests.
Existing apostrophe parser produces balanced strong/em nodes and sanitizes surrounding inline content.
Blank lines and recognized blocks flush paragraph/list/definition state; expanded structures use the same AST pipeline.
Full MediaWiki list continuation, complete definition grammar, unrestricted table attributes, and complete file/category semantics remain outside the bounded subset.

KnownLimitations: No complete MediaWiki 1.45 structural or HTML parity claim.
Definition-list same-line continuation and advanced list continuation are outside the subset.
Heading IDs remain governed by existing conventions; this renderer does not introduce a new ID scheme.
Database-backed authorization, historical source acquisition, Cargo parity, Lua worker certification, and migration readiness remain independent gates.
RecommendedNextMilestone: Run the full structural regression and then audit any remaining renderer differences against independently captured reference HTML without changing production evidence or security boundaries.
